new_value: Fixed both flagged shifts in response_replay_update() (oscore_protect.c) with explicit uint64_t intermediate arithmetic per modern style, comments added: (1) newest-seq branch: *window = shift >= 32 ? 1U : (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)*window << shift) | 1U) — the old (*window << shift) promoted uint32_t to signed int making bit-31 participation formal UB; uint64 math truncated back is bit-identical for every previously-defined input (shift < 32 guaranteed by the ternary, >= 32 collapses to 1 exactly as before). (2) in-window branch: *window |= diff >= 32 ? 0U : (uint32_t)((uint64_t)1 << diff) — old 1U << diff was defined only for diff < 32 (guaranteed by callers via response_replay_acceptable with REPLAY_WINDOW range 16..32, i.e. zero observable change on the reachable domain) but formally undefined otherwise; now defined everywhere. Legacy oscore_replay.c:161 pattern deliberately untouched (out-of-blast-radius per scope; verified unchanged in source). response_replay_acceptable() line 83 bare-1U shift left as-is: unsigned int shift by < 32 is fully defined, no promotion hazard. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Wshift-count-overflow clean on oscore_protect.c at default and max Kconfig configs; no PRIu64/format-string drift (helper contains no format usage); token greps confirm old signed-promotion idiom absent and guard idiom present.
